ops.selectConn: Select a ClickHouse connection in the sidebar.
ops.notClickHouse: Operations reads ClickHouse's own system tables. "{name}" is not a ClickHouse connection.
ops.title: ClickHouse Operations
ops.scopeHint: Every view reads each replica with clusterAllReplicas('{cluster}', ...), and Stop acts ON CLUSTER.
ops.refreshingEvery: Refreshing every {seconds} s. Click to pause.
ops.pausedHint: Paused. Click to refresh every few seconds.
ops.monitorHint: Make a monitor of these numbers, sampled every minute and kept for a day. This panel says what the server is doing now; a monitor says when it started.
ops.connectToSee: Connect "{name}" in the sidebar to see what it is doing.
ops.noMatch: Nothing in the last day matches "{filter}".

remote.readsAll: It reads everything {source} returns and writes it into {target}. Nothing is copied back the other way.
remote.noSort: Nothing has been described or previewed yet, so the table is created with no sort order (tuple()). Describe it first and it is sorted by its first column.
remote.sortedBy: Sorted by {column}, its first column. The Storage tab is where a MergeTree is then made to behave.
remote.notClickHouse: Remote data reads ClickHouse's table functions. "{name}" is not a ClickHouse connection.
remote.title: Remote data
remote.connectToRead: Connect "{name}" in the sidebar to read from somewhere else.
remote.keyHint: A saved account's key is read from the keychain when the statement runs, and never reaches this screen or query history.
remote.name: Name
remote.mergeTreeSorted: MergeTree, sorted by {column}. Everything the source returns is read once and written here.
remote.unsortedHint: Describe it first and the table is sorted by its first column; without that it is created unsorted.

columnsRead.one: {count} column, as the server read them
columnsRead.other: {count} columns, as the server read them

storage.notInSystem: {name} is not in system.tables on this server.
storage.noParts: A {engine} table keeps no parts on disk, so it has no partitions, projections or skip indexes.
storage.noSystemParts: This server does not expose system.parts to this user.
storage.oldProjections: This server is older than system.projections (ClickHouse 24.x), so projections cannot be listed.
storage.noSkipIndices: This server does not expose system.data_skipping_indices to this user.
storage.noClauses: This engine takes no key, partition or TTL clause.
storage.rowsHint: What the catalog says, which for a MergeTree table is exact.
storage.partsIntro: Every INSERT writes a part and merges combine them.
storage.partsClean: Nothing is waiting to be cleaned up.
storage.partsPending: {n} more have been merged away and not yet deleted, which is normal.
storage.granulesHint: A granule is the smallest thing a read can skip; the sort key's index has one entry per granule.
storage.partitionsBlurb: A partition is read and dropped as a unit, and its parts are what merges combine. Too many parts in one partition slows inserts, then refuses them.
storage.noPartsYet: No parts: this table has no rows on this node yet.
storage.projectionsBlurb: A projection is a second copy of this table kept in another order, or pre-aggregated. ClickHouse reads it instead of the table when that reads less.
storage.noneProjections: None. A recurring heavy aggregation over this table is usually what one is for.
storage.skipBlurb: ClickHouse has no B-tree. These hold one summary per group of granules, and a filter on a column outside the sort key skips granules only if one of them says it can.
